content: Hi everyone, hopefully this is the right place to post this. I'm curious if there's a way to access the tactics used in a proof (to maybe be lifted and applied in another proof) as opposed to just directly accessing the proof object. Thanks!
Can you perhaps make a small example of what you're after?

Are you looking for the syntax of the whole tactic sequence, something like an array of individual tactics, or something else? The general answer is that this stuff is present in the infotree but not in the elaborated expression (which is just the proof term, or what you call the proof object).

I was looking to extract the syntax of the whole tactic sequence. It seems I actually don't need to do this (and it doesn't seem like this would be very idiomatic approach) :upside_down:. But thank you both for your help! I'll remember to check the infotree if it comes up again.
